guarantees.claim: In StIdle, if !app_active_i and sw_cmd_i == CmdStart, next state is StMsgFeed; otherwise stays StIdle.
In StMsgFeed, if sw_cmd_i == CmdProcess, next state is StProcessing; otherwise stays StMsgFeed.
In StProcessing, if sha3_absorbed_i is true (strict mubi4 test), next state is StAbsorbed; otherwise stays StProcessing.
In StAbsorbed, if sw_cmd_i == CmdManualRun, next state StSqueezing; else if CmdDone, next state StIdle; else stays StAbsorbed.
In StSqueezing, if keccak_done_i, next state StAbsorbed; otherwise stays StSqueezing.
In StTerminalError, next state remains StTerminalError (terminal state).
Any state not explicitly enumerated (including invalid encodings) transitions to StTerminalError via the unique case default.
guarantees.cond: st not in {StIdle, StMsgFeed, StProcessing, StAbsorbed, StSqueezing, StTerminalError}

guarantees.claim: If lc_escalate_en_i is true (loose test), next state is unconditionally forced to StTerminalError, overriding all previous state transition logic.
If the next state after case and escalation logic is not StTerminalError and clear_after_error_i is true (strict mubi4 test), next state is forced to StIdle.

assumptions.claim: External logic must issue sw commands (Start, Process, ManualRun, Done) only when the FSM is in the expected state as per protocol; otherwise the command is silently ignored.
assumptions.cond: always, but critical at state transitions
assumptions.risk: If a command is issued at the wrong time, the FSM may miss it, causing functional hang or incorrect sequence.

assumptions.claim: lc_escalate_en_i must be a properly encoded multi-bit lifecycle signal such that lc_tx_test_true_loose only asserts when a genuine escalation is intended.
assumptions.risk: A spurious or false assertion will lock the FSM in StTerminalError, causing denial of service and possible loss of ongoing operations.

assumptions.claim: clear_after_error_i must be a valid mubi4 encoding and only asserted true when the system is ready to fully clear error and return to Idle, with all sensitive state properly wiped by other logic.
assumptions.risk: An unexpected assertion could prematurely force the FSM to Idle, potentially discarding in-progress operations and leaving uncleared sensitive data in other modules.

uncertain_points.claim: The clear_after_error_i override forces the FSM to StIdle from any non-terminal state, but it is unclear whether this FSM transition alone guarantees that all sensitive data (partial messages, keys) within the kmac_errchk module or wider system is cleared before returning to Idle.
uncertain_points.risk: If other modules are not simultaneously cleared, sensitive state could persist, violating secure wipe requirements.

uncertain_points.claim: The start condition requires !app_active_i along with CmdStart. The role and timing of app_active_i are undefined in this chunk; it is unclear whether its assertion should prevent starting or represents an alternate mode.
uncertain_points.cond: st == StIdle and app_active_i is true
uncertain_points.risk: If app_active_i is intended to gate start for a specific reason (e.g., application vs. software control), misunderstanding could lead to missed commands or deadlock.
